deduct.empty: {name} has no stars right now – deducting works again once there are some.
deduct.title: Taking stars away – sparingly and on purpose
deduct.one: One star at a time at most. A fixed price (“hitting costs three stars”) turns into arithmetic: whoever has enough stars buys their way out.
deduct.zero: Never below zero. With debts no reward is in reach any more – then nothing pays off, not even the good things.
deduct.praise: Praise first: for every deduction, four or more stars for what went well.
deduct.calm: Calmly and right away, with a short reason. The reason stays in the history, so the child can read later what it was for.
deduct.moreTitle: And if one star is not enough?
deduct.more: Then making amends helps more than a bigger deduction: the child does something good for the other one – comforting, helping, giving something back. Create a one-off task for it; with it the child earns the star back. For worse things, a consequence outside the stars belongs to it, such as a break or a talk.
deduct.correction: Stars booked by mistake are corrected in the admin under star history.
